fields.summary: Add deprecation status columns to I_S.SYSTEM_VARIABLES

issuetype.description: A new feature of the product, which has yet to be developed.
issuetype.name: New Feature

fields.description:
Previously one could already do:
{code:sql}
SELECT VARIABLE_NAME, GLOBAL_VALUE, DEFAULT_VALUE
  FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SYSTEM_VARIABLES
  WHERE GLOBAL_VALUE_ORIGIN IN('CONFIG', 'SQL');
{code}
Which would show all variables specifically set in the server's config or using SQL. For example:
{noformat:title=CS 13.0.1 3a2f8e27981b76b99d2b87cc3bcec5ef022b2b23 (Debug, Clang 21.1.3-20250923) Build 10/04/2026}
13.0.1-dbg>set global sql_mode='';
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.000 sec)

13.0.1-dbg>SELECT VARIABLE_NAME, GLOBAL_VALUE, DEFAULT_VALUE   FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SYSTEM_VARIABLES   WHERE GLOBAL_VALUE_ORIGIN IN('CONFIG', 'SQL');
+---------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| VARIABLE_NAME | GLOBAL_VALUE | DEFAULT_VALUE                                                                             |
+---------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| SQL_MODE      |              | STRICT_TRANS_TABLES,ERROR_FOR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO,NO_AUTO_CREATE_USER,NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION |
+---------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
1 row in set (0.012 sec)
{noformat}
This feature adds {{IS_DEPRECATED='YES'}}, which allows for easy / automated "is this server's [config/SQL] setting some deprecated variables" checks by running:
{code:sql}
SELECT VARIABLE_NAME, GLOBAL_VALUE, DEFAULT_VALUE
  FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SYSTEM_VARIABLES
  WHERE GLOBAL_VALUE_ORIGIN IN('CONFIG', 'SQL')
  AND IS_DEPRECATED = 'YES';
{code}
For example:
{code:sql}
13.0.0-opt>set global sql_mode='';
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.000 sec)

13.0.0-opt>set global TX_READ_ONLY=on;
Query OK, 0 rows affected, 1 warning (0.000 sec)

13.0.0-opt>SELECT VARIABLE_NAME, GLOBAL_VALUE, DEFAULT_VALUE   FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SYSTEM_VARIABLES   WHERE GLOBAL_VALUE_ORIGIN IN('CONFIG', 'SQL');  # Set vars
+---------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| VARIABLE_NAME | GLOBAL_VALUE | DEFAULT_VALUE                                                                             |
+---------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| TX_READ_ONLY  | ON           | OFF                                                                                       |
| SQL_MODE      |              | STRICT_TRANS_TABLES,ERROR_FOR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO,NO_AUTO_CREATE_USER,NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION |
+---------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
2 rows in set (0.002 sec)

13.0.0-opt>SELECT VARIABLE_NAME, GLOBAL_VALUE, DEFAULT_VALUE   FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SYSTEM_VARIABLES   WHERE GLOBAL_VALUE_ORIGIN IN('CONFIG', 'SQL') AND IS_DEPRECATED = 'YES';  # Set vars which are depreciated
+---------------+--------------+---------------+
| VARIABLE_NAME | GLOBAL_VALUE | DEFAULT_VALUE |
+---------------+--------------+---------------+
| TX_READ_ONLY  | ON           | OFF           |
+---------------+--------------+---------------+
1 row in set (0.002 sec)
{code}

comments.body:
Hello team, I made a small pull request for this feature.
Here is a link: https://github.com/MariaDB/server/pull/4698

PTAL!

[~hholzgra] is there a reason you wanted an IS_DEPRECATED boolean, rather than a NULLable string of the system variable replacement?

Looking at [~HNOONa-0]'s draft they are explicitly doing a {{var->option.deprecation_substitute != NULL}} to make it a boolean. A more functional alternate would be just returning the string and leaving it to the user to use "DEPRECATED_REPLACEMENT IS NOT NULL". Word suggestions on a better name than "DEPRECATED_REPLACEMENT" appreciated. "REPLACED_BY"? "SUPERCEDED_BY"?).

Having additional replacement information for settings where just an old name was deprecated in favor of a newer on would be nice, too.

But the majority of deprecated settings are ones that we want to drop completely, not just rename / replace, right?

So how would {{DEPRECATED_REPLACEMENT IS NOT NULL}} help with the "up for complete removal in a future release" case? The replacement information should still be NULL in that case.

So in my ideal world we would have both IS_DEPRECATED as a boolean, and DEPRECATED_REPLACEMENT as additional information on those settings where IS_DEPRECATED is TRUE

https://github.com/MariaDB/server/pull/4698 ready for testing (after as small commit message improvement).

Thanks for your input [~hholzgra] and [~HNOONa-0] for implementing this.

I would not consider this redundant, "is it deprecated" and "it was renamed to this" are two different things that just overlap.

Things could be made more clear by making {{IS_DEPRECATED}} an ENUM with VALUES "NO"/"YES"/"RENAMED"; but the new name would still require a 2nd column then

Ack on YES/NO. {{RENAMED}} seems redundant as you can use {{OR DEPRECATED_REPLACEMENT IS NOT NULL}} is really required.

Note deprecated replacement isn't necessary just a varable - 10.11 has {{wsrep_causal_reads}} -> {{@@wsrep_sync_wait=1}}.

I wasn't quite sure about the one-column idea. Ok, two columns it is.

I was not suggesting YES/NO/RENAMED for the reason that [~danblack] mentioned — it's not necessarily a rename.
So, the first column is YES/NO. [~danblack], see how other YES/NO columns are done, there's {{store_yesno()}} helper and {{Yes_or_empty()}} in the {{sysvars_fields_info}} array.

[~HNOONa-0], thanks for much for updating it.

The update copies the small bit of {{READ_ONLY}} code in the same function on the same table to provide {{YES}}/{{NO}}.


[~HNOONa-0], can I trouble you to:

Have a {{sql/sql_i_s.h}} as a {{Yes_or_no}} (with capitalized YES/NO) class like {{Yes_or_empty}} with subsequent changes for {{READ_ONLY}}, {{IS_DEPRECATED}} in {{sql/set_var.cc}}.

And optionally:

Changes to use the new {{Yes_or_no}} and remove {{store_yesno}} in {{sql/sql_show.cc}} can be left as separate commit or the back of your PR. Or this can be left as a later cleanup MDEV if you don't want to do this part.

Note, but not to be fixed, this highlights a discrepancy that {{Yes_or_empty}} has {{Yes}} but the {{READ_ONLY}}/{{IS_DEPRECATED}} is capitalized {{YES}}/{{NO}}. We've released these so we shouldn't change them.

Hi team, thanks for followup.

I think i will separate the refactor with respect to `store_yesno` into its own pull request. Since the new feature still needs to be tested and isn't guaranteed to be merged, isolating the refactor changes is better.
Sure. Thank you. All good for testing from me.

[~HNOONa-0], Notice this made the 13.0 preview release! Thank you.

https://mariadb.org/mariadb-13-0-preview-now-available/

[~raghunandan.bhat] has left some PR comments, that will need to be addressed before a merge into the 13.0.1 release.

Summary of what's been done so far - this is being in done in two commits:
first commit - refactoring
- Rename {{Yes_or_empty}} into {{Yes_or_no}} and update {{::value()}} so that it returns {{YES / NO}} instead of {{Yes / ""}}. The reason being, a {{Yes_or_empty}} column uses {{store_yesno()}} to fill those columns for almost all cases (with few exceptions).
- Remove {{store_yesno()}} everywhere and use {{Yes_or_no::value()}} instead. 
- For columns that have already been released with non-standard output (like {{Yes / ""}}), do not use {{Yes_or_no::value()}}. Instead use {{val ? "Yes" : ""}}. This is for {{I_S.COLLATIONS}} ({{IS_DEFAULT}} and {{IS_COMPILED}} columns) and {{I_S.COLLATION_CHARACTER_SET_APPLICABILITY}} ({{IS_DEFAULT}} column) tables with a comment that this is a historical exception kept for backward compatibility.
- {{I_S.SEQUENCES.CYCLE_OPTION}} column was returning {{0 / 1}} despite being defined as a {{YES / NO}} type, which was a bug. It is now updated to return  {{YES / NO}} to align with the SQL standard.

second commit
- new feature to add {{IS_DEPRECATED}} and {{DEPRECATION_REPLACEMENT}} columns to {{I_S.SYSTEM_VARIABLES}} table.

[~raghunandan.bhat] Hi! What is the branch to test please? Have there been changes to the patch since {{preview-13.0-preview}}? If so please provide a new test branch, on par with main/trunk plus the new patch. Thanks!

With some git commands back and forth got a 13.0 branch based on:
{noformat}
commit cb6cebe4ed0630beed9f18f3c3e0ae14847434cf
Author: HNOONa-0 <hanyahmed11811@gmail.com>
Date:   Wed Mar 25 22:27:48 2026 +0200

    MDEV-35369: Add IS_DEPRECATED to SYSTEM_VARIABLES
    
    - Add IS_DEPRECATED and DEPRECATION_REPLACEMENT columns to the
      SYSTEM_VARIABLES information schema table
    - Add a mysql-test case to verify the new columns output correctly

commit 1294aae6a5bcf339c81db8aebccdb583058dbdee
Author: HNOONa-0 <hanyahmed11811@gmail.com>
Date:   Wed Mar 25 21:41:13 2026 +0200

    MDEV-35369: Refactor Yes_or_empty to Yes_or_no
    
    - Rename Yes_or_empty to Yes_or_no, returning YES/NO instead of Yes/"".
    - Globally replace store_yesno() with Yes_or_no::value().
    - Preserve legacy output ("Yes"/"") in I_S.COLLATIONS and
      I_S.COLLATION_CHARACTER_SET_APPLICABILITY for backward compatibility.
    - Assign CYCLE_OPTION variable "Yes"/"No" values
{noformat}
[~raghunandan.bhat] [~danblack] Please confirm this is all correct.

Please note that the query in the original descriptiption will list *all* deprecated variables:

{noformat:title=MDEV-35369 CS 13.0.0 cb6cebe4ed0630beed9f18f3c3e0ae14847434cf (Optimized, Clang 21.1.3-20250923) Build 01/04/2026}
13.0.0-opt>SELECT VARIABLE_NAME, GLOBAL_VALUE, DEFAULT_VALUE FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SYSTEM_VARIABLES WHERE GLOBAL_VALUE_ORIGIN IN('CONFIG', 'SQL', 'COMPILE-TIME') AND IS_DEPRECATED = 'YES';
+------------------------------------------+-----------------+-----------------+
| VARIABLE_NAME                            | GLOBAL_VALUE    | DEFAULT_VALUE   |
+------------------------------------------+-----------------+-----------------+
| METADATA_LOCKS_HASH_INSTANCES            | 8               | 8               |
| INNODB_BUFFER_POOL_CHUNK_SIZE            | 0               | 0               |
| OPTIMIZER_ADJUST_SECONDARY_KEY_COSTS     | 0               | 0               |
| LOG_SLOW_ADMIN_STATEMENTS                | ON              | ON              |
| TX_READ_ONLY                             | OFF             | OFF             |
| INNODB_LRU_FLUSH_SIZE                    | 0               | 32              |
| INNODB_PREFIX_INDEX_CLUSTER_OPTIMIZATION | OFF             | OFF             |
| INNODB_FILE_PER_TABLE                    | ON              | ON              |
| METADATA_LOCKS_CACHE_SIZE                | 1024            | 1024            |
| OLD_PASSWORDS                            | OFF             | OFF             |
| INNODB_PURGE_RSEG_TRUNCATE_FREQUENCY     | 128             | 128             |
| INNODB_LOG_SPIN_WAIT_DELAY               | 0               | 0               |
| SQL_NOTES                                | ON              | ON              |
| BINLOG_OPTIMIZE_THREAD_SCHEDULING        | ON              | ON              |
| INNODB_FT_ENABLE_DIAG_PRINT              | OFF             | OFF             |
| INNODB_FLUSH_METHOD                      | O_DIRECT        | O_DIRECT        |
| ALTER_ALGORITHM                          | DEFAULT         | DEFAULT         |
| TX_ISOLATION                             | REPEATABLE-READ | REPEATABLE-READ |
+------------------------------------------+-----------------+-----------------+
18 rows in set (0.002 sec)
{noformat}

i.e. one would have to manually scan through the results to see if this server's config is specifically setting/changing some deprecated variables. Alternatively, one can run:

{code:sql}
SELECT VARIABLE_NAME, GLOBAL_VALUE, DEFAULT_VALUE 
 FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SYSTEM_VARIABLES 
 WHERE GLOBAL_VALUE_ORIGIN IN('CONFIG', 'SQL', 'COMPILE-TIME') 
 AND GLOBAL_VALUE != DEFAULT_VALUE 
 AND IS_DEPRECATED = 'YES';
{code}

This query yields only deprecated variables which had their settings modified/changed, for example:

{noformat:title=MDEV-35369 CS 13.0.0 cb6cebe4ed0630beed9f18f3c3e0ae14847434cf (Optimized, Clang 21.1.3-20250923) Build 01/04/2026}
13.0.0-opt>SELECT VARIABLE_NAME, GLOBAL_VALUE, DEFAULT_VALUE FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SYSTEM_VARIABLES WHERE GLOBAL_VALUE_ORIGIN IN('CONFIG', 'SQL', 'COMPILE-TIME') AND GLOBAL_VALUE != DEFAULT_VALUE AND IS_DEPRECATED = 'YES';
+-----------------------+--------------+---------------+
| VARIABLE_NAME         | GLOBAL_VALUE | DEFAULT_VALUE |
+-----------------------+--------------+---------------+
| INNODB_LRU_FLUSH_SIZE | 0            | 32            |
+-----------------------+--------------+---------------+
1 row in set (0.003 sec)
{noformat}
Incidentally, the {{INNODB_LRU_FLUSH_SIZE}} setting will likely always show, ref:
https://mariadb.com/docs/server/server-usage/storage-engines/innodb/innodb-system-variables#innodb_lru_flush_size
Documented at https://mariadb.com/docs/server/reference/system-tables/information-schema/information-schema-tables/information-schema-system_variables-table

The query *from the description* will only list values modified in the *CONFIG* file and from the *SQL*. It will not list variables that are at their *COMPILE-TIME* values. Of course, if you *modify the original query* and add {{'COMPILE-TIME'}} to the condition, you'll also see unmodified variables, that's true.
Do we need {{DEPRECATED_REPLACEMENT}} column? It's always NULL in all tests. I'd suggest to drop it

items.toString:
Previously one could already do:
{code:sql}
SELECT VARIABLE_NAME, GLOBAL_VALUE, DEFAULT_VALUE
  FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SYSTEM_VARIABLES
  WHERE GLOBAL_VALUE_ORIGIN IN('CONFIG', 'SQL')
  AND IS_DEPRECATED = 'YES';
{code}
Which would show all variables specifically set in the server's config or using SQL. For example:
{noformat:title=CS 13.0.1 3a2f8e27981b76b99d2b87cc3bcec5ef022b2b23 (Debug, Clang 21.1.3-20250923) Build 10/04/2026}
13.0.1-dbg>set global sql_mode='';
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.000 sec)

+---------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| VARIABLE_NAME | GLOBAL_VALUE | DEFAULT_VALUE                                                                             |
+---------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| SQL_MODE      |              | STRICT_TRANS_TABLES,ERROR_FOR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO,NO_AUTO_CREATE_USER,NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION |
+---------------+--------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
1 row in set (0.012 sec)
{noformat}
This feature adds IS_DEPRECATED='YES', which allows for easy / automated "is this server's [config/SQL] setting some deprecated variables" checks by running:
{code:sql}
SELECT VARIABLE_NAME, GLOBAL_VALUE, DEFAULT_VALUE
  FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SYSTEM_VARIABLES
  WHERE GLOBAL_VALUE_ORIGIN IN('CONFIG', 'SQL')
  AND IS_DEPRECATED = 'YES';
{code}

fields.summary: Add Centos Stream 10 as a CI builder

issuetype.description: A task that needs to be done.
issuetype.name: Task

fields.description:
We should prepare for Centos 10 stream builder and ensure an easy transition.

This task covers the addition of the following:
* CentOS 10 stream builder on amd64, aarch64, ppc64le

The builder will run the following tests:
* autobake package building
* Comprehensive mtr runs, as for previous release package distros
* Install & Upgrade tests

As this will have to be done before we migrate to the new buildbot system, we will have this MDBF as part of the "Migration to new buildbot" epic.
Given that this task will have to be completed before the migration to new buildbot is complete, it is part of this particular epic.

fields.description:
centos7 has gcc 4.8 which can no longer compile 11.8

we need a new bintar builder in addition to centos7. centos7 will build 11.7-, and new one will build 11.8+

Using debian 10 might be a good idea, because aarch bintars are built on debian 10.

This *must* be done before the next release

11.7 does not build on the centos-7 bintar builder anymore either, so maybe it's just easier to switch to the new one instead of keeping fixing the old one. 
In any case it's just one release, so it's not important.

As for Debian 10, it's strange to start building on something that is already EOL, and the Debian 10 repositories are probably already unavailable. Maybe better something that is still alive, e.g. Rocky Linux 8?

Sure.

Note, that we still need to keep centos7 for 10.5–11.4 releases and debian 10, I suppose, too.

Hi.

[~serg] , [~elenst]

According to the bintar specs https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ky5ekpJSfo9ZRHKOro4B6z7wv5b1SoOvbmgj7RoyirQ/edit?tab=t.kotmz2b4c7fl
I've created a bintar docker image based on almalinux-8.

The Pull Request for submitting this image can be found at https://github.com/MariaDB/buildbot/pull/690 and was assigned for review at [~cvicentiu].

In parallel, I will prepare the buildbot configuration changes (builder, worker).
When these changes will reach buildbot.dev.mariadb.org , I can test 11.7 and 11.8 and share the resulting packages with all of you. 
*This way we can all inspect the packages and agree if the builder is good or not.*

Thanks.

[~cvicentiu]
Pushed factory changes to https://github.com/MariaDB/buildbot/pull/690

[~serg] [~elenst] [~cvicentiu]

Tested the new bintar in buildbot.*dev*.mariadb.org
Below are the results. If you are ok with them I can deploy them on *buildbot.mariadb.org* starting next week.

*11.8*
- Build: [amd64-almalinux-8-bintar|https://buildbot.dev.mariadb.org/#/builders/532/builds/2]
- Binary tarball: https://ci.dev.mariadb.org/90/amd64-almalinux-8-bintar/mariadb-11.8.0-linux-systemd-x86_64.tar.gz

*11.7*
- Build: [amd64-almalinux-8-bintar|https://buildbot.dev.mariadb.org/#/builders/532/builds/3]
- Binary tarball: https://ci.dev.mariadb.org/101/amd64-almalinux-8-bintar/mariadb-11.7.2-linux-systemd-x86_64.tar.gz
I suppose [~rvarzaru] or [~cvicentiu] verified that these packages satisfy requirements as per gdoc? Set of plugins, dynamic dependencies, all ok?
[~cvicentiu] developed a script to validate it, I think he can answer this one based on the packages that I've generated in the previous comments.

[~serg] [~cvicentiu]
The new bintar was deployed in production, see: https://buildbot.mariadb.org/#/builders/857
if you consider that other changes are needed , just let me know and I will handle it asap.

How do you package {{libgalera_smm.so}} ?

Why is it listed twice?

No, they were always added manually in the prepare-release script.

I didn't like that, I wanted buildbot to produce ready-to-release packages, so I implemented {{-DEXTRA_FILES}} option.

But it was never actually used, prep script was still replacing galera files in the bintars — because this was the only way to make sure bintars get the latest galera.

I still think it's better to have buildbot to produce ready packages, and I don't like that bintars are tested with old galera but released with newer one, not something they were tested with. But to make it happen you need to create some process to make sure the galera in the bintar builders is always the latest one. Let's do it in a separate issue, it's not "reproducing old buildbot", because old buildbot never did that.

[~serg]

For the new-bintar, because we have an automated process to generate the builder,
I thought of this before, and I handled it here: https://github.com/MariaDB/buildbot/blob/dev/ci_build_images/bintar.Dockerfile

{code:java}
&& dnf config-manager --add-repo https://ci.mariadb.org/galera/mariadb-4.x-latest-gal-${ARCH}-rhel${VERSION_ID}.repo \
and then install galera-4
{code}

This is the latest galera produced for amd64-rhel-8 by the dedicated galera builder.
We don't have an alma-linux-8 galera builder as of now, I know packages between rhel-8 / alma-linux 8 should be compatible.

As for centos-7-bintar is not so easy to maintain because it's EOL so maybe there you'll be ok with the "re-packaging" method :)

I opened https://jira.mariadb.org/browse/MDBF-935 to track current problems. cc: [~cvicentiu]
I'm having a hard time to make libncurses.a behave properly on centos-7 so that all the required functions are found in the static library, it's not the case for the new bintar (there I can fix it) .

I will keep you up to date on MDBF-935.

comments.body:
[~elenst] To whom I can speak with to get a copy of /kvm/vms/vm-centos74-amd64-build.qcow2 for myself from old-buildbot? I don't have access to the underlying infra.

And any idea who was updating GnuTLS in old-buildbot? Maybe some scripts were saved and I don't have to repeat the painful experience of compiling GnuTLS from source.

I thought somebody from the Foundation already went through this step. [~faust] maybe?
If not, the answer to both questions is Daniel Bartholomew.

Well, I have this, but this is from the time where the version from the CentOS 7 repos was suitable for our needs.
Now, I need to compile it from source, guess the same thing was done on old-bb. I'll ask dbart.


{code:java}
#!/bin/bash

rpm -qa --qf '%{NAME}\n' |sort>packages_before
yum install -y rpm-build yum-utils
yumdownloader --source gnutls-devel
yum-builddep -y gnutls-*.src.rpm
rpm -ivh gnutls-*.src.rpm
sed -i 's/--disable-static/--enable-static \\\n--disable-tests/g' ~/rpmbuild/SPECS/gnutls.spec
sed -i 's/export LDFLAGS="-Wl,--no-add-needed"/export LDFLAGS="-Wl,--copy-dt-needed-entries -fpic -fPIC"/g' ~/rpmbuild/SPECS/gnutls.spec
sed -i 's/make %{?_smp_mflags}/make %{?_smp_mflags} CFLAGS="-fpic -fPIC" CXX_FLAGS="-fpic -fPIC"/g' ~/rpmbuild/SPECS/gnutls.spec
rpmbuild -bc ~/rpmbuild/SPECS/gnutls.spec
mkdir -p local/lib
mv -v ~/rpmbuild/BUILD/gnutls-*/lib/.libs/libgnutls.a local/lib
comm -13 packages_before <(rpm -qa --qf '%{NAME}\n' |sort)|xargs rpm -evh
#rm -rf ~/rpmbuild gnutls-*.src.rpm packages_before

{code}

[~elenst] [~cvicentiu]
I've made some tests locally with the updated version of GnuTLS (compiled statically).

11.4 -> ok
11.7 - > although GnuTLS version is ok, compilation is failing with:


{code:java}
[  4%] Building CXX object tpool/CMakeFiles/tpool.dir/aio_linux.cc.o
In file included from /home/buildbot/11.7/include/my_sys.h:20:0,
                 from /home/buildbot/11.7/tpool/aio_linux.cc:25:
/home/buildbot/11.7/include/m_string.h:225:13: error: missing space between '""' and suffix identifier
 LEX_CSTRING operator""_LEX_CSTRING(const char *str, size_t length)
             ^
make[2]: *** [tpool/CMakeFiles/tpool.dir/aio_linux.cc.o] Error 1

{code}

I see that buildbot.mariadb.net also complains about it. See: https://buildbot.mariadb.net/buildbot/builders/kvm-bintar-centos74-amd64/builds/14300

This was first introduced in: https://github.com/MariaDB/server/commit/4d9548876e1654f86301d284af1b795c6b5bacfc

Could it be the classic "too old compiler" ?

[~elenst]

I was able to install gcc (GCC) 9.3.1 20200408 (Red Hat 9.3.1-2) and newer GnuTLS (from old-bb, 3.7.0). << + provider_bzip2.so and provider_lzo.so >> 
in the *centos-7-bintar* container image (build the image locally for now, soon testing in DEV)

*and I was able to compile server verions: 10.6 ,10.11, 11.4, 11.7, 11.8 successfully.* 
The choice for the compiler is based on what I can find in the *centos-release-scl* repositories (devtoolset packages which include a newer GCC).

The discussion is also on Slack regarding this observation:
https://mariadb.slack.com/archives/C012UURLW9W/p1737103059422229?thread_ts=1736951352.629539&cid=C012UURLW9W

Is this approach OK for you and [~serg] ?
If yes, I can proceed making tests in DEV and share the results with you before deploying to buildbot.mariadb.org

This does not remove the need of a new bintar builder, but I know there are some pending discussions and decisions for which [~cvicentiu] already shared with you a whole very well detailed document.

Until new bintar specs are sorted out, bumping GCC on CentOS 7 is what I can do the fastest. 
It's still a maintenance burden, therefore, we do not take responsibility for its maintenance in the future.
[~serg] [~elenst] ok with you to bump gcc on centos7 - builder for now so we can build on 11.7 / 11.8 ?

I have no opinion on the subject of bintars, as was previously discussed, I leave it to Sergei and Vicentiu to decide on the matter.
JIRA-wise, as long as MDBF-866 remains an open blocker, I read the situation as "there is no need to update the compiler on CentOS 7, and there is the need to create a new builder".

Agree. It makes no sense to update the compiler on CentOS 7.

Either we'll decide to live by the old rule, then old bintars will stay on CentOS 7, and new releases will use a new bintar builder.
Or we'll change the rule and all bintars will move to a new builder based on some non-EOL-ed distro.
There is no option "stay on CentOS 7 but upgrade the compiler" as far as I can see

[~serg]
my idea was to quickly update Centos 7 to support 11.7/11.8 for the upcoming releases
so we have enough time focusing on a new bintar builder specs, either, as you said, for all bintars or just for new releases, to be decided.

I proposed this because by the time the new builder specs are ready and agreed it might be too late and to close to the release.

One can find the gnutls.sh script in https://github.com/MariaDB/buildbot/blob/dev/ci_build_images/scripts/gnutls.sh


{code:java}
FROM quay.io/mariadb-foundation/bb-worker:centos7-bintar

USER root

RUN mkdir /changelog

COPY gnutls.sh /changelog
COPY Dockerfile /changelog

WORKDIR /scripts

RUN yum remove -y gnutls-devel gnutls \
    && rm -f /scripts/local/lib/libgnutls.a \
    && chmod +x /changelog/gnutls.sh \
    && /changelog/gnutls.sh \
    && yum -y install bzip2-devel lzo-devel \
    && rm -rf /root/* \
    && rm -rf /root/.ccache \
    && rm -f /scripts/*.src.rpm*

WORKDIR /buildbot
USER buildbot
{code}

issuetype.description: A task that needs to be done.
issuetype.name: Task

fields.description:
LDD minor upgrade tests fail on 10.6 with a different dependency.

Affected builders: RHEL 8 and 9.

{code}
====== Package MariaDB-server-debuginfo
-=== /usr/lib/debug/usr/lib64/mysql/plugin/ha_spider.so-10.6.20-1.el8.aarch64.debug
+=== /usr/lib/debug/usr/lib64/mysql/plugin/ha_spider.so-10.6.21-1.el8.aarch64.debug
{code}

The ldd diff script should be adjusted to account for the version number change.

comments.body:
[~elenst]
Do you have any idea why this might happen? I don't really understand the + , - statically linked.

10.11 - aarch64-rhel-8-rpm-autobake-minor-upgrade-all
https://buildbot.mariadb.org/#/builders/733/builds/198/steps/3/logs/stdio

-=== /usr/lib/debug/usr/lib64/mysql/plugin/ha_spider.so-10.11.10-1.el8.aarch64.debug
-	statically linked

10.6 - amd64-rhel-8-rpm-autobake-minor-upgrade-all
https://buildbot.mariadb.org/#/builders/743/builds/178/steps/3/logs/stdio
+=== /usr/lib/debug/usr/lib64/mysql/plugin/ha_spider.so-10.6.21-1.el8.x86_64.debug
+	statically linked

[~elenst] [~cvicentiu]

On the following example:
*Builder*: amd64-rhel-8-rpm-autobake-minor-upgrade-all
*MariaDB Server version*: 10.6
*Link to Build*: https://buildbot.mariadb.org/#/builders/743/builds/178/steps/3/logs/stdio
*Error:*

{code:java}
+=== /usr/lib/debug/usr/lib64/mysql/plugin/ha_spider.so-10.6.21-1.el8.x86_64.debug
+	statically linked

{code}

I reproduced it locally in a RHEL8 VM and somewhere in the *upgrade script log* when we run manually, we have:

{code:java}
ldd: warning: you do not have execution permission for `/usr/lib/debug/usr/lib64/mysql/plugin/ha_spider.so-10.6.21-1.el8.x86_64.debug'
{code}


*Let's see:*

{code:java}
[buildbot@bb-ro-apexis-bbw03-x64-rhel-8-amd64 scripts]$ ldd /usr/lib/debug/usr/lib64/mysql/plugin/ha_spider.so-10.6.21-1.el8.x86_64.debug
ldd: warning: you do not have execution permission for `/usr/lib/debug/usr/lib64/mysql/plugin/ha_spider.so-10.6.21-1.el8.x86_64.debug'
	statically linked
[buildbot@bb-ro-apexis-bbw03-x64-rhel-8-amd64 scripts]$ echo $?
0
{code}


*The return code is 0* so:

{code:java}
 sudo ldd "$f" > /dev/null 2>&1 || continue 
{code}

*has NO EFFECT.*
Making 
{code:java}
echo "=== $f" >> "./ldd-${suffix}.${old_or_new}"
{code}
 *run even if is not the case. -> False-Positive ERROR.*

*I'll give myself execute permissions.*

{code:java}
[buildbot@bb-ro-apexis-bbw03-x64-rhel-8-amd64 scripts]$ ldd /usr/lib/debug/usr/lib64/mysql/plugin/ha_spider.so-10.6.21-1.el8.x86_64.debug
	statically linked
[buildbot@bb-ro-apexis-bbw03-x64-rhel-8-amd64 scripts]$ echo $?
0
{code}


*Still, nothing valuable.*

And now I start to wonder. From a few picks, *it looks like DEBUGINFO  packages have no dynamic executable.*
Let's take a few examples by looking into the *LDD generated files*. You see, everywhere we analyse a *debuginfo* package, *there's NO ACTUAL LDD output.*


{code:java}
 === /usr/bin/replace
 ====== Package MariaDB-client-debuginfo
 ====== Package MariaDB-common
 === /usr/lib64/mysql/plugin/auth_gssapi_client.so

 ====== Package MariaDB-cracklib-password-check-debuginfo
 ====== Package MariaDB-devel

 === /usr/lib64/libmysqlclient.so
 ====== Package MariaDB-devel-debuginfo
 ====== Package MariaDB-gssapi-server
 === /usr/lib64/mysql/plugin/auth_gssapi.so
 ====== Package MariaDB-gssapi-server-debuginfo
 ====== Package MariaDB-oqgraph-engine
{code}

 
 I can conclude that the SPIDER differences come from the fact that our LDD analyzer script *is not a one-fit-all solutin and sometimes can generate false-positives.*
 My suggestion is to exclude from analysis the debuginfo packages. What do you say [~cvicentiu] [~elenst]

I don't think it is related to our ldd analyzer script. It is either {{ldd}} or our linking that behaves strangely, I can't say which it is.

The test shows a difference because there is indeed a difference.

Here is the example from https://buildbot.mariadb.org/#/builders/743/builds/178/steps/3/logs/stdio link (10.6 on x86_64) above. I've tried the file from the last 10.6.20 release package vs the buildbot package, on the same machine:

{noformat:title=10.6.20}
$ ldd ha_spider.so-10.6.20-1.el8.x86_64.debug 
ldd: warning: you do not have execution permission for `./ha_spider.so-10.6.20-1.el8.x86_64.debug'

$ echo $?
1

$ file ha_spider.so-10.6.20-1.el8.x86_64.debug
ha_spider.so-10.6.20-1.el8.x86_64.debug: ELF 64-bit LSB shared object, x86-64, version 1 (SYSV), dynamically linked, BuildID[sha1]=66e3e1becdabbfeb87d4f4894f4b7cc32bb18a15, with debug_info, not stripped

$ ls -l ha_spider.so-10.6.20-1.el8.x86_64.debug 
-r--r--r--. 1 buildbot buildbot 6629824 Jan 15 11:59 ha_spider.so-10.6.20-1.el8.x86_64.debug
{noformat}
{noformat:title=10.6.21}
$ ldd ha_spider.so-10.6.21-1.el8.x86_64.debug 
ldd: warning: you do not have execution permission for `./ha_spider.so-10.6.21-1.el8.x86_64.debug'
	statically linked

$ echo $?
0

$ file ha_spider.so-10.6.21-1.el8.x86_64.debug 
ha_spider.so-10.6.21-1.el8.x86_64.debug: ELF 64-bit LSB shared object, x86-64, version 1 (SYSV), dynamically linked, BuildID[sha1]=3978165c0a6351e055cf19c873e1eb4f992c0dce, with debug_info, not stripped

$ ls -l ha_spider.so-10.6.21-1.el8.x86_64.debug 
-r--r--r--. 1 buildbot buildbot 6618208 Jan 15 11:57 ha_spider.so-10.6.21-1.el8.x86_64.debug
{noformat}

So, the files have seemingly the same permissions, {{file}} shows both as dynamically linked; but on 10.6.20 {{ldd}} returns an error silently (so the script collecting dependencies skips the file), while on 10.6.21 it says "statically linked" and succeeds, so the script includes the output. 
Warning about permissions don't affect the outcome, in the above I've kept the permissions "as is" for certainty, but making them executable doesn't change anything, the difference is still the same, only without a warning.

I don't have an aarch machine handy to check the other case, but I guess it's the same there, only the other way round.

[~elenst] indeed that's the case. I checked buildbot.mariadb.net for comparison but it seems that the ldd.{old,new} files are empty.

Even if it shows a difference for the failed builders, it defeats the purpose of the LDD test, because, at least for buildbot.mariadb.org, there's no output for debuginfo packages when running LDD (except these special cases).

I'm not sure how to continue from this point on.
[~elenst] now I saw your last comment on page refresh, sorry.
Opened https://github.com/MariaDB/buildbot/pull/682

[~cvicentiu] [~elenst]
Deployed the changes on buildbot.mariadb.org.
Builders are green, see below. I will mark this issue as fixed but if you still notice ha_spider related issue feel free to re-open it.

Thanks!


{code:java}
MariaDB Server 10.6 
--------------------
--------------------
Old: https://buildbot.mariadb.org/#/builders/733/builds/183 (aarch64-rhel-8-rpm-autobake-minor-upgrade-all)
	Issue: 
		-=== /usr/lib/debug/usr/lib64/mysql/plugin/ha_spider.so-10.6.20-1.el8.aarch64.debug
		+=== /usr/lib/debug/usr/lib64/mysql/plugin/ha_spider.so-10.6.21-1.el8.aarch64.debug
New (re-run of old): https://buildbot.mariadb.org/#/builders/733/builds/207
	Builder Green: program finished with exit code 0


MariaDB Server 10.11
--------------------
--------------------
Old: https://buildbot.mariadb.org/#/builders/733/builds/198 (aarch64-rhel-8-rpm-autobake-minor-upgrade-all)
	Issue:
		-=== /usr/lib/debug/usr/lib64/mysql/plugin/ha_spider.so-10.11.10-1.el8.aarch64.debug
		-	statically linked
New (re-run of old): https://buildbot.mariadb.org/#/builders/733/builds/208 (aarch64-rhel-8-rpm-autobake-minor-upgrade-all)
	Builder Green: program finished with exit code 0
	
Same change should apply successfully to RHEL 9 also.
{code}
Deployed the changes in Production, builders are green.

My findings on the NOT OK builders:

{code:java}
(2/2) Installing: MariaDB-columnstore-engine-10.11.11_6.4.8-1.x86_64 [..
 
Mariab Columnstore uninstall completed

/usr/bin/mcsGetConfig: symbol lookup error: /usr/lib64/libjoblist.so: undefined symbol: EVP_CIPHER_get_iv_length

[~elenst] Then we let it fail and it will be resolved over time when SLES packages will be released from buildbot.mariadb.org ?
I agree to you that it makes no sense to install SLES SP3 packages on the SP6 that we have.

Currently the test doesn't know that the packages provided are from SP3, doesn't have any information that .NET buildbot has an SP3 VM.
What I want to know if it's OK to start releasing .ORG buildbot packages, meaning SLES 15 Sp6.

fields.summary: Galera feature: retry applying of write sets at slave nodes

issuetype.description: A new feature of the product, which has yet to be developed.
issuetype.name: New Feature

fields.description:
A new Galera feature that allows retrying of applying of writesets at
slave nodes (codership/mysql-wsrep-bugs/#1619). Currently replication
applying stops for first non ignored failure occurring in event
applying, and node will do emergency abort (or start inconsistency
voting). Some failures, however, can be concurrency related, and
applying may succeed if the operation is tried at later time.
    
This feature introduces a new dynamic global option variable
{{wsrep_applier_retry_count}} that controls the retry-applying feature:
a zero value disables retrying and a positive value sets the maximum
number of retry attempts. The default value for this option is zero,
which means that this feature is disabled by default.

fields.description:
Given that we have 5 s390x VM instances, each configured with 8vCPU's, we need to consider lowering the number of parallel builds on each VM from 3 to 1.

The builds are running Make with a parallel of 7 thus the 1 build per VM.
This can be achieved by updating the global lock file in worker_locks.yaml

Queues might grow a bit but at the same time having proper CPU -> build allocation will make builds faster and much more stable (minimize chances of timeouts during packaging or unstable MTR tests which are sensible on time).

fields.summary: New-style hint: [NO_]ROWID_FILTER

issuetype.description: A new feature of the product, which has yet to be developed.
issuetype.name: New Feature

fields.description:
Add a new-style hint to control Rowid Filters.

{code:sql}
/* +ROWID_FILTER( [table_name [index_name [ ...] ]]) */
/* +NO_ROWID_FILTER([table_name [index_name [ ... ] ]] ) */
{code}

h2. Hint applicability 

Like {{NO_RANGE_OPTIMIZATION}} or {{MRR}}, the hint can apply to
* Query block  - {{NO_ROWID_FILTER()}} 
* Table  - {{NO_ROWID_FILTER(table_name)}}
* Specific index(es)  - {{NO_ROWID_FILTER(table_name index1 index2 ...}} 

h2. Semantics

h3. Semantics of NO_ROWID_FILTER 

Do not consider Rowid Filter for the scope of the hint (all tables in the query block, specific table, specific index(es)).

h2. Semantics of ROWID_FILTER

This should do something like "force use of ROWID_FILTER for the {{table.index}} it targets" but there are some issues:

h3. Possible semantics #1

At query block or table level it makes sense to have the meaning just "enable use of ROWID_FILTER". Assuming it is disabled globally.  

h3. Possible semantics #2

At index level, it would be nice to force use of indexes regardless of the costs. 
That is,
{code:sql}
SELECT /*+ ROWID_FILTER(t1 idx1) */ 
{code}

would force the use of Rowid Filter made from t1.idx1  if the picked plan allows it, regardless of the costs.

h3. A problem?
Suppose we have implemented the logic:

{quote}
{{ROWID_FILTER(t1 idx1)}} makes the optimizer to use RowidFilter(idx1) if the access method to t1 allows it.
{quote}
Then we run some query Q without any hints.
Suppose the optimizer's choice is to use index idx2 for accessing table t1. 
Then we add the {{ROWID_FILTER(t1 idx1)}} to the Q and run it.
When the optimizer looks for access method to t1, it picks idx2 and adds rowid filter(t1) .
This makes the const higher than just using idx2. 
Use of {{idx2+RowidFilter(idx1)}} may become more expensive than e.g. full table scan.
Or the join order may change.

That is, the effect of the {{ROWID FILTER(t1 idx1)}} hint may be that some totally different plan will be used.

h2. ...
TODO: 

- When creating potential Rowid filters, only consider the specified indexes.  

- the ROWID_FILTER hint doesn't affect the choice of access method.
  If the optimizer picks an index for which this rowid filter can be applied, good. If not, not our problem.

- When considering whether to use the rowid filter together with an index, 
  make a cost-based choice between specified filters.

There are some ideas about specifying the buffer size available for the rowid filter but they are outside of the scope of this MDEV.

comments.body:
[~psergei], I have a suggestion for the "Possible semantics #2" concern: we can follow   [the rule for other index level hints | https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/optimizer-hints.html#optimizer-hints-index-level], i.e. enable or disable the specified index or indexes, the same way as FORCE INDEX, IGNORE INDEX do.
For example, ROWID_FILTER(t1 key1,key2) will enable rowid filtering only for `key1` and `key2` of table `t1` but not any other key.   NO_ROWID_FILTER(t1 key1) will disable rowid filtering for `key1` but all other keys will be available.

For now I decided to finalize the feature with this limitation:
{code}
===== Interaction with other index hints =====
    If [NO_]INDEX, [NO_]JOIN_INDEX hints are specified for the same table,
    then only indexes whitelisted by INDEX() or JOIN_INDEX() can be considered
    for rowid filters. ROWID_FILTER() hint cannot force the use of indexes that are
    disabled by NO_INDEX() / NO_JOIN_INDEX() or omitted from INDEX() / JOIN_INDEX().
    For example, if one index should be used for data access and another for
    a rowid filter, the filter index must be mentioned in both hints:
      SELECT /*+ index(t1 key_a, key_b) rowid_filter(t1 key_b) a FROM t1 ....
{code}

The pull request https://github.com/MariaDB/server/pull/4275  is ready for review.
The patch is ok to go.  Hint interpretation has the described limitations.
Branch for testing: MDEV-36089-rowid-flt.
[~lstartseva], old-style index hints are processed only if new-style hints are not specified. So, since `ROWID_FILTER()` is an index hint, `FORCE INDEX(key_b)` is effectively ignored.
Testing done, Ok to push
Pushed into *main* ([commit|https://github.com/MariaDB/server/commit/8e9213da94e66545c58681f4e631a87ab020b4c1]).

Documented here (and below): https://mariadb.com/docs/server/ha-and-performance/optimization-and-tuning/optimizer-hints#no_rowid_filter
[~oleg.smirnov] Please review.

[~stefan.hinz], first I tried to make some clean-ups myself but gave up as there is a lot of what I'd like to change.

Here is my suggestions:
# (minor) Why is `optimizer-hints.md`  located at /server/reference/sql-statements/data-manipulation/selecting-data/?   I believe `/server/ha-and-performance/optimization-and-tuning/query-optimizations/`  would be a better location, for example `optimizer-switch.md` and other optimizer-related things are placed there.
# I would not mix new-style (so called `expanded`) and old-style hints in one page.  Currently there is some kind of chaos (for example, ROWID_FILTER, SPLIT_MATERIALIZED are put in the old-style section).  Let's create a new page for new-style hints.
# Ideally, our documentation for hints should look like https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/optimizer-hints.html.  It's well organized, has clear structure and hyper-links. With hints we basically repeat the same functionality that MySQL already has, so in terms of context almost everything is applicable for us. It would be OK if you just copy-paste their page (adjusting formatting, hyper-links, maybe changing some wordings, etc) and then I'll proof-read it and clean it up.
Documented here: https://mariadb.com/docs/server/ha-and-performance/optimization-and-tuning/optimizer-hints/expanded-optimizer-hints#no_rowid_filter

fields.description:
Implement table-level hints:
{code}
MERGE, NO_MERGE 
DERIVED_CONDITION_PUSHDOWN, NO_DERIVED_CONDITION_PUSHDOWN
{code}

in the same way they're done in MySQL 8.  See MySQL docs at:
https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/derived-condition-pushdown-optimization.html
https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/optimizer-hints.html#optimizer-hints-table-level

The logic for enabling the hints is expected to be very basic - hook at the same place where the check for optimizer_switch is, override the optimizer_switch setting.

The code to base on is MDEV-35504, look at other similar level hints and copy the approach.

comments.body: All changes are delivered to 12.0-mdev-36106-no-derived-condition-pushdown-hint branch for these hints, including tests.
[~Gosselin] is it possible to create pull requests for those? IIRC it was possible to make pull requests against non-main branches...

[~psergei] Yes, I will make them, it's no problem.  

EDIT:  PR is here, https://github.com/MariaDB/server/pull/3870
Thanks [~psergei], I didn't know about {{json_detailed}}.  Will do!
[~oleg.smirnov] maybe this is related to the {{TABLE_LIST}} hint API that I added, I will check.

[~oleg.smirnov] we indeed produce warnings for the wrong_name example you gave above.  But we don't include the wrong name hints in the Note message for the query.  That's because the hints are stored by table name and when we fix the hints, we look them up only by the table alias, which must be known because it is associated with a TABLE instance.  We don't find the wrong names at that point because they don't have TABLEs that exist, so they are not fixed.  Later, during warning generation, we skip any unfixed hints (see Opt_hints::print).
{code}
MariaDB [test]> explain extended   SELECT /*+ no_derived_condition_pushdown(wrong_name) */a, b FROM      (SELECT i as a, j as b FROM          (select i*10 as i, j*5 as j from v1) dt_in) AS dt_out   WHERE a < 3 AND b > 8;
+------+-------------+-------+------+---------------+------+---------+------+------+----------+-------------+
| id   | select_type | table | type | possible_keys | key  | key_len | ref  | rows | filtered | Extra       |
+------+-------------+-------+------+---------------+------+---------+------+------+----------+-------------+
|    1 | SIMPLE      | t1    | ALL  | NULL          | NULL | NULL    | NULL | 10   |   100.00 | Using where |
+------+-------------+-------+------+---------------+------+---------+------+------+----------+-------------+
1 row in set, 2 warnings (5.091 sec)

MariaDB [test]> show warnings\G
*************************** 1. row ***************************
  Level: Warning
   Code: 4209
Message: Unresolved table name `wrong_name`@`select#1` for NO_DERIVED_CONDITION_PUSHDOWN hint
*************************** 2. row ***************************
  Level: Note
   Code: 1003
Message: select `test`.`t1`.`i` * 10 AS `a`,`test`.`t1`.`j` * 5 AS `b` from `test`.`t1` where `test`.`t1`.`i` * 10 < 3 and `test`.`t1`.`j` * 5 > 8
2 rows in set (0.001 sec)
{code}

We can alter this behavior by removing this check from the start of Opt_hints::print:
{code}
  /* Do not print the hint if we couldn't attach it to its object */
  if (!is_fixed())
    return;
{code}

If we do that, then we generate warnings like this:
{code}
MariaDB [test]> explain extended   SELECT /*+ no_derived_condition_pushdown(wrong_name) */a, b FROM      (SELECT i as a, j as b FROM          (select i*10 as i, j*5 as j from v1) dt_in) AS dt_out   WHERE a < 3 AND b > 8;
+------+-------------+-------+------+---------------+------+---------+------+------+----------+-------------+
| id   | select_type | table | type | possible_keys | key  | key_len | ref  | rows | filtered | Extra       |
+------+-------------+-------+------+---------------+------+---------+------+------+----------+-------------+
|    1 | SIMPLE      | t1    | ALL  | NULL          | NULL | NULL    | NULL | 10   |   100.00 | Using where |
+------+-------------+-------+------+---------------+------+---------+------+------+----------+-------------+
1 row in set, 2 warnings (0.010 sec)

MariaDB [test]> show warnings\G
*************************** 1. row ***************************
  Level: Warning
   Code: 4209
Message: Unresolved table name `wrong_name`@`select#1` for NO_DERIVED_CONDITION_PUSHDOWN hint
*************************** 2. row ***************************
  Level: Note
   Code: 1003
Message: select /*+ NO_DERIVED_CONDITION_PUSHDOWN(`wrong_name`@`select#1`) */ `test`.`t1`.`i` * 10 AS `a`,`test`.`t1`.`j` * 5 AS `b` from `test`.`t1` where `test`.`t1`.`i` * 10 < 3 and `test`.`t1`.`j` * 5 > 8
2 rows in set (0.001 sec)
{code}
[~Gosselin], it's fine that we don't print unresolved or invalid hints in the expanded query text (warning level "Note"). No need to change this behavior.

Hey [~oleg.smirnov], thank you for your thoughtful feedback.  To address your concern, I want to mention a comment at the top of that code block you cited which I've copied here for convenience:
{code}
This instance will have been marked as fixed on the basis of its
attachment to a SELECT_LEX (during get_qb_hints) but that is
insufficient to consider it fixed for the case where a TABLE
instance is required but not yet available.  If the associated
table isn't yet fixed, then reset this instance's fixed value to
DELAYED.  Later, during fix_hints_for_table(TABLE*), the hint and
its corresponding TABLE instance will be marked with fixed=FIXED.
{code}
To expand on that comment a bit:
# opt_hints_table has not yet been created at the point where it is needed at call-sites (see table.cc:10116 where this new method fix_hints_for_table is called)
# opt_hints_qb does exist and can be used to temporarily fix hints for the table, by setting them to the DELAYED state where they'll be properly fixed later
# temporarily fixing hints relies on TABLE_LIST which does not (as you correctly pointed out) have everything needed to avoid putting hints into the DELAYED state
# A post-condition of Opt_hints_qb::fix_hints_for_table is that Opt_hints_qb instances will be in the DELAYED state, unless they're fixed and their corresponding Opt_hints_table instance exists and is also fixed.

Before my change, fixing hints for tables relied on Opt_hints_qb::fix_hints_for_table(TABLE*) overload implementation.  My new overload for that method, Opt_hints_qb::fix_hints_for_table(TABLE_LIST*) is implemented at the same layer in the abstraction. Table-level hint fixing is also done on Opt_hints_qb instance (see the setup_tables function in sql_base.cc).  There, in setup_tables, we check if query block hints are initialized and if there is no opt_hints_table, then create the new opt_hints_table instance by calling fix_hints_for_table.  I'm doing the same, but adding to the condition that the opt_hints_table instance may not exist or if it does, that hints were delayed.

A consequence of my approach with TABLE_LIST appears to be the missing warning that you point out.  Maybe that can be fixed?  Or maybe it is a limitation of the hints architecture?  I'm looking to see how we can solve that problem.

I was able to eliminate the DELAYED logic after your insight regarding index-level hints:  since hints fixed with TABLE_LIST cannot be index-level, due to lack of key information at that point in processing, there is no need for DELAYED logic and a later re-fixing of hints once TABLE instances are available.  With that refactoring, the above query handles both NO_MERGE hints correctly:
{code}
explain extended SELECT /*+ NO_MERGE(dt2) NO_MERGE(dt)*/ * FROM
(SELECT i as a, j as b FROM t1) AS dt, (SELECT i as a, j as b FROM t1) AS dt2
WHERE dt.a = dt2.a and dt.b = dt2.b AND dt.a < 3 AND dt.b > 8;
id	select_type	table	type	possible_keys	key	key_len	ref	rows	filtered	Extra
1	PRIMARY	<derived2>	ALL	NULL	NULL	NULL	NULL	10	100.00	Using where
1	PRIMARY	<derived3>	ref	key0	key0	16	dt.a,dt.b	1	100.00	
3	DERIVED	t1	ALL	NULL	NULL	NULL	NULL	10	100.00	Using where
2	DERIVED	t1	ALL	NULL	NULL	NULL	NULL	10	100.00	Using where
{code}
The case where both tables are merged:
{code}
explain extended SELECT /*+ MERGE(dt2) MERGE(dt)*/ * FROM
(SELECT i as a, j as b FROM t1) AS dt, (SELECT i as a, j as b FROM t1) AS dt2
WHERE dt.a = dt2.a and dt.b = dt2.b AND dt.a < 3 AND dt.b > 8;
id	select_type	table	type	possible_keys	key	key_len	ref	rows	filtered	Extra
1	SIMPLE	t1	ALL	NULL	NULL	NULL	NULL	10	100.00	Using where
1	SIMPLE	t1	ALL	NULL	NULL	NULL	NULL	10	100.00	Using where; Using join buffer (flat, BNL join)
{code}
Alternating MERGE/NO_MERGE works as you'd expect.
I updated the PR with the latest changes to include this test case as well as removing both unneeded DELAYED hint processing and DELAYED hint marking, so the new API for fixing hints with TABLE_LISTs fixes them immediately rather than relying on a later re-fixing stage.

Testing done. Ok to push.
But, there is MDEV-37020 and if derived table merge optimization is enabled, possible, it will be necessary to check hints MERGE/NO_MERGE for update/delete again.

Documented here: https://mariadb.com/docs/server/ha-and-performance/optimization-and-tuning/optimizer-hints/expanded-optimizer-hints#derived_condition_pushdown-and-no_derived_condition_pushdown and https://mariadb.com/docs/server/ha-and-performance/optimization-and-tuning/optimizer-hints/expanded-optimizer-hints#merge-and-no_merge.

fields.summary: Optimizer support for functional indexes: handle GROUP/ORDER BY

issuetype.description: A new feature of the product, which has yet to be developed.
issuetype.name: New Feature

fields.description:
See MDEV-35615, section *Support ORDER BY/GROUP BY*:
{quote}
We need to rewrite ORDER BY vcol_expr into ORDER BY vcol_field so that the optimizer can use an index to skip sorting.
(MySQL does this, this should be easy to do)
{quote}

h2. Contents

{quote}
1. Rewrite makes covering indexes non-covering
1.1 Solving the Rewrite-makes-indexes-non-covering problem
1.1.1 Execution code doesnt re-compute stored VCOLs
1.1.2 Working around execution code shortcomings.
2. ShouldRewriteModifyAllFields problem
{quote}

h2. 1. Rewrite makes covering indexes non-covering
Consider a testcase:
{code:sql}
create table t (c int, d varchar(100), index IDX_C(c));
insert into t select seq,seq from seq_1_to_10000;
alter table t
  add column vc int as (c + 1),
  add index IDX_VC(vc);
{code}
A query using vcol_expr will use index-only scan on IDX_C :
{code}
explain select c+1 from t order by c+1 limit 2;
+------+-------------+-------+-------+---------------+-------+---------+------+-------+-----------------------------+
| id   | select_type | table | type  | possible_keys | key   | key_len | ref  | rows  | Extra                       |
+------+-------------+-------+-------+---------------+-------+---------+------+-------+-----------------------------+
|    1 | SIMPLE      | t     | index | NULL          | IDX_C | 5       | NULL | 10330 | Using index; Using filesort |
+------+-------------+-------+-------+---------------+-------+---------+------+-------+-----------------------------+
{code}
(and will not  consider IDX_VC).
If we do rewrite in ORDER BY, it will use  IDX_VC, but in a non-index-only way:
{code}
MariaDB [j4]> explain select c+1 from t order by vc limit 2;
+------+-------------+-------+-------+---------------+--------+---------+------+------+-------+
| id   | select_type | table | type  | possible_keys | key    | key_len | ref  | rows | Extra |
+------+-------------+-------+-------+---------------+--------+---------+------+------+-------+
|    1 | SIMPLE      | t     | index | NULL          | IDX_VC | 5       | NULL | 2    |       |
+------+-------------+-------+-------+---------------+--------+---------+------+------+-------+
{code}
neither IDX_C, nor IDX_VC are covering anymore. 

That is, rewriting  {{ORDER BY vcol_expr}} into {{ORDER BY vcol_field}} makes covering indexes non-covering.

(TODO: what about the rewrite done in MDEV-35616? Won't it have the same problem? )

h3. 1.1 Solving the Rewrite-makes-indexes-non-covering problem

It seems, the problem is that the optimizer is not aware that it has an option to compute {{vcol_field}} from {{vcol_expr}}. 

What if we made it aware about that?  We could take the code that computes the set of covering indexes and make sure
that  {{vcol_field}} returns these indexes as covering:
* indexes that include {{vcol_field}}   -- this is already done now
*  {{(vcol_expr)->covering_keys}}  -- this is new

Then,  changing {{vcol_expr}} to {{vcol_field}} would not reduce the set of query's covering_keys.

h4. 1.1.1 Execution code doesnt re-compute stored VCOLs
Can we do it?  Not yet: the execution side is missing some code: 
https://mariadb.slack.com/archives/C021E77G7K2/p1746525196637819

It seems, for stored virtual columns it is missing the logic to  "if the employed access method didn't read the value for column VCOL, compute the value of VCOL from VCOL_EXPR" .

h4. 1.1.2 Working around execution code shortcomings (NOT NEEDED?)

What if we only handled non-stored virtual columns? That is:
1. Solve the Rewrite-makes-indexes-non-covering problem for non-stored vcols  (vcol_field->covering_keys would include vcol->expr->covering_keys).
2. Do the ORDER BY rewrite only for non-stored virtual columns.

h2. 2. ShouldRewriteModifyAllFields problem

ORDER BY clause is processed as follows:

The item is added in JOIN::all_fields.
The item is added into JOIN::ref_pointer_array.
The ORDER BY expression in the ORDER structure points to an element in the JOIN::ref_pointer_array.

We do rewrite by changing the element in JOIN::ref_pointer_array.  However, the element in JOIN::all_fields remains unchanged.  Should it be changed?

I have a patch that changes it. It can cause a problem.
{code:sql}
create table t1 (a int, b int);
insert into t1 select seq, seq from seq_1_to_1000;
alter table t1 add vcol int as (a+1), add index(vcol);

explain 
select (a+1),b from t1 order by 1 limit 2;
select (a+1),b from t1 order by 1 limit 2;
{code}

Current ORDER BY code (b91a6da292550b26d8e1901eaf72086465476459):
{code}
MariaDB [test]> select (a+1),b from t1 order by 1 limit 2;
+-------+------+
| (a+1) | b    |
+-------+------+
|     2 |    1 |
|     3 |    2 |
+-------+------+
{code}
code that changes all_fields : https://gist.github.com/spetrunia/c6eb87344ef992f99455ff73e8c8e327.  causes this: column name becomes vcol:
{code}
MariaDB [j1]> select (a+1),b from t1 order by 1 limit 2;
+------+------+
| vcol | b    |
+------+------+
|    2 |    1 |
|    3 |    2 |
+------+------+
{code}
I'm not sure if that's the only issue.

(note the LIMIT):

Note that for the purpose of comparison in the following approaches we do not consider existing tests.

problem or implement this:

[~ycp], I couldn't help wondering why so debugged the above a little bit.
The table is
{code:sql}
CREATE TABLE `t3` (
  `a` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `b` int(11) GENERATED ALWAYS AS (-`a`) VIRTUAL,
  `c` int(11) GENERATED ALWAYS AS (-`a`) VIRTUAL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`a`),
  UNIQUE KEY `c` (`c`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_uca1400_ai_ci
{code}
and we're debugging the select for:
{code}
MariaDB [test]> explain select b from t3 where c > -3 order by b;
+------+-------------+-------+-------+---------------+------+---------+------+------+------------------------------------------+
| id   | select_type | table | type  | possible_keys | key  | key_len | ref  | rows | Extra                                    |
+------+-------------+-------+-------+---------------+------+---------+------+------+------------------------------------------+
|    1 | SIMPLE      | t3    | range | c             | c    | 5       | NULL | 2    | Using where; Using index; Using filesort |
+------+-------------+-------+-------+---------------+------+---------+------+------+------------------------------------------+
1 row in set (0.006 sec)
{code}

When doing table read, I saw TABLE::update_virtual_fields() to update the value for column b.

However, the plan uses filesort.  filesort's strategy is "read all the columns from the table, then sort them, then return them in sorted order".
I don't see the the column b saved.
And, we don't recompute it when reading filesort's output.

Why does filesort not save the value of b? because it's not in the table->read_set when we are in
filesort|Sort_param::init_for_filesort|get_addon_fields.

And it is not there, because it was removed by the piece of logic here:
In JOIN::optimize_stage2|JOIN::init_join_cache_and_keyread|TABLE::mark_index_columns.

Not yet sure what to do about this...

Thanks for the analysis which I can observe. I also spent some time to understand the difference of the test outcome between innodb and myisam. It is caused by differences in table flags and index flags, but that seems less important.

Given that my latest solution updates the read_set to include the vcols when doing the vcol calculation in keyread of "non-conventional" keys covering vcols, perhaps we could move such updates earlier, around the time of the call to table->mark_index_columns(table->file->keyread, table->read_set) in JOIN::init_join_cache_and_keyread. items.toString:
See MDEV-35615, section *Support ORDER BY/GROUP BY*:
{quote}
We need to rewrite ORDER BY vcol_expr into ORDER BY vcol_field so that the optimizer can use an index to skip sorting.
(MySQL does this, this should be easy to do)
{quote}

h2. Problem: rewrite makes covering indexes non-covering
Consider a testcase:
{code:sql}
create table t (c int, d varchar(100), index IDX_C(c));
insert into t select seq,seq from seq_1_to_10000;
alter table t
  add column vc int as (c + 1),
  add index IDX_VC(vc);
{code}
A query using vcol_expr will use index-only scan on IDX_C :
{code}
explain select c+1 from t order by c+1 limit 2;
+------+-------------+-------+-------+---------------+-------+---------+------+-------+-----------------------------+
| id   | select_type | table | type  | possible_keys | key   | key_len | ref  | rows  | Extra                       |
+------+-------------+-------+-------+---------------+-------+---------+------+-------+-----------------------------+
|    1 | SIMPLE      | t     | index | NULL          | IDX_C | 5       | NULL | 10330 | Using index; Using filesort |
+------+-------------+-------+-------+---------------+-------+---------+------+-------+-----------------------------+
{code}
(and will not  consider IDX_VC).
If we do rewrite in ORDER BY, it will use  IDX_VC, but in a non-index-only way:
{code}
MariaDB [j4]> explain select c+1 from t order by vc limit 2;
+------+-------------+-------+-------+---------------+--------+---------+------+------+-------+
| id   | select_type | table | type  | possible_keys | key    | key_len | ref  | rows | Extra |
+------+-------------+-------+-------+---------------+--------+---------+------+------+-------+
|    1 | SIMPLE      | t     | index | NULL          | IDX_VC | 5       | NULL | 2    |       |
+------+-------------+-------+-------+---------------+--------+---------+------+------+-------+
{code}
neither IDX_C, nor IDX_VC are covering anymore. 

That is, rewriting  {{ORDER BY vcol_expr}} into {{ORDER BY vcol_field}} makes covering indexes non-covering.

(TODO: what about the rewrite done in MDEV-35616? Won't it have the same problem? )

h2. Solving the Rewrite-makes-indexes-non-covering problem

It seems, the problem is that the optimizer is not aware that it has an option to compute {{vcol_field}} from {{vcol_expr}}. 

What if we made it aware about that?  We could take the code that computes the set of covering indexes and make sure
that  {{vcol_field}} returns these indexes as covering:
* indexes that include {{vcol_field}}   -- this is already done now
*  {{(vcol_expr)->covering_keys}}  -- this is new

Then,  changing {{vcol_expr}} to {{vcol_field}} would not reduce the set of query's covering_keys.

Can we do it?  Not yet: the execution side is missing some code: 
https://mariadb.slack.com/archives/C021E77G7K2/p1746525196637819

It seems, for stored virtual columns it is missing the logic to  "if the employed access method didn't read the value for column VCOL, compute the value of VCOL from VCOL_EXPR" .

insert into t select seq,seq from seq_1_to_10000;
alter table t
  add column vc int as (c + 1),
  add index IDX_VC(vc);
{code}
A query using vcol_expr will use index-only scan on IDX_C :
{code}
explain select c+1 from t order by c+1 limit 2;
+------+-------------+-------+-------+---------------+-------+---------+------+-------+-----------------------------+
| id   | select_type | table | type  | possible_keys | key   | key_len | ref  | rows  | Extra                       |
+------+-------------+-------+-------+---------------+-------+---------+------+-------+-----------------------------+
|    1 | SIMPLE      | t     | index | NULL          | IDX_C | 5       | NULL | 10330 | Using index; Using filesort |
+------+-------------+-------+-------+---------------+-------+---------+------+-------+-----------------------------+
{code}
(and will not  consider IDX_VC).
If we do rewrite in ORDER BY, it will use  IDX_VC, but in a non-index-only way:
{code}
MariaDB [j4]> explain select c+1 from t order by vc limit 2;
+------+-------------+-------+-------+---------------+--------+---------+------+------+-------+
| id   | select_type | table | type  | possible_keys | key    | key_len | ref  | rows | Extra |
+------+-------------+-------+-------+---------------+--------+---------+------+------+-------+
|    1 | SIMPLE      | t     | index | NULL          | IDX_VC | 5       | NULL | 2    |       |
+------+-------------+-------+-------+---------------+--------+---------+------+------+-------+
{code}
neither IDX_C, nor IDX_VC are covering anymore. 

That is, rewriting  {{ORDER BY vcol_expr}} into {{ORDER BY vcol_field}} makes covering indexes non-covering.

(TODO: what about the rewrite done in MDEV-35616? Won't it have the same problem? )

h3. 1.1 Solving the Rewrite-makes-indexes-non-covering problem

It seems, the problem is that the optimizer is not aware that it has an option to compute {{vcol_field}} from {{vcol_expr}}. 

What if we made it aware about that?  We could take the code that computes the set of covering indexes and make sure
that  {{vcol_field}} returns these indexes as covering:
* indexes that include {{vcol_field}}   -- this is already done now
*  {{(vcol_expr)->covering_keys}}  -- this is new

Then,  changing {{vcol_expr}} to {{vcol_field}} would not reduce the set of query's covering_keys.

h4. 1.1.1 Execution code doesnt re-compute stored VCOLs
Can we do it?  Not yet: the execution side is missing some code: 
https://mariadb.slack.com/archives/C021E77G7K2/p1746525196637819

It seems, for stored virtual columns it is missing the logic to  "if the employed access method didn't read the value for column VCOL, compute the value of VCOL from VCOL_EXPR" .

h4. 1.1.2 Working around execution code shortcomings (NOT NEEDED?)

What if we only handled non-stored virtual columns? That is:
1. Solve the Rewrite-makes-indexes-non-covering problem for non-stored vcols  (vcol_field->covering_keys would include vcol->expr->covering_keys).
2. Do the ORDER BY rewrite only for non-stored virtual columns.

h2. 2. ShouldRewriteModifyAllFields problem

ORDER BY clause is processed as follows:

The item is added in JOIN::all_fields.
The item is added into JOIN::ref_pointer_array.
The ORDER BY expression in the ORDER structure points to an element in the JOIN::ref_pointer_array.

We do rewrite by changing the element in JOIN::ref_pointer_array.  However, the element in JOIN::all_fields remains unchanged.  Should it be changed?

I have a patch that changes it. It can cause a problem.
{code:sql}
create table t1 (a int, b int);
insert into t1 select seq, seq from seq_1_to_1000;
alter table t1 add vcol int as (a+1), add index(vcol);

explain 
select (a+1),b from t1 order by 1 limit 2;
select (a+1),b from t1 order by 1 limit 2;
{code}

Current ORDER BY code (b91a6da292550b26d8e1901eaf72086465476459):
{code}
MariaDB [test]> select (a+1),b from t1 order by 1 limit 2;
+-------+------+
| (a+1) | b    |
+-------+------+
|     2 |    1 |
|     3 |    2 |
+-------+------+
{code}
code that changes all_fields : https://gist.github.com/spetrunia/c6eb87344ef992f99455ff73e8c8e327.  causes this: column name becomes vcol:
{code}
MariaDB [j1]> select (a+1),b from t1 order by 1 limit 2;
+------+------+
| vcol | b    |
+------+------+
|    2 |    1 |
|    3 |    2 |
+------+------+
{code}
I'm not sure if that's the only issue.
This issue is part of TODO-5311

fields.summary: Protected branches worker hosts are fully loaded

issuetype.description: A task that needs to be done.
issuetype.name: Task

fields.description:
Recently getting a lot of OOM conditions in which libvirt VM's on hz-bbw4 are the victims of a too much Docker load on this machine.

This led to analyzing the theoretical load on the protected branches worker hosts, hz-bbw1 and hz-bbw4 and it doesn't surprise me that we assign more builders than the infrastructure allows us to do.

I propose to add hz-bbw7 as a protected branches worker host, as on hz-bbw7 currently only bintar (centos7, almalinux-8) run and we have enough room.

More on that, if multiple tarball's are triggered in a short amount of time, is a safer choice to decrease the locks value on hz-bbw 1,4,7 so that we don't risk over-provisioning builds.

    - CPU: 64
    - MEM: 128 G
hz-bbw1:
    - CPU: 64
    - MEM: 128 G
-------------------------------------------------
Per host Docker Request CPU: 97

fields.summary: Refactor buildbot internals to drop docker-latent-worker

issuetype.description: A task that needs to be done.
issuetype.name: Task

fields.description:
h2. Scope

This task covers the refactoring work required to move from {{DockerLatentWorker}} to an equivalent of "RunVM", only for Docker containers.

h3. Motivation
The use of {{DockerLatentWorker}} as a base for defining environments in buildbot was a bad design decision. There are numerous limitations with this approach:

* It is impossible to define a single DockerLatentWorker as an "environment" (for instance Debian 12 Build Environment), then use it across multiple physical machines.
** To get this to work, one must define "environment" clones for each physical machine we allocate to use "DockerLatentWorkers". That is why we currently have:
*** {{aarch64-bbw\[1-6\]-docker-debian-11}}
*** {{aarch64-bbw\[1-6\]-docker-debian-12}}
If one more physical machine is added to buildbot, all these DockerLatentWorkers must be cloned with a 7 in their name.
* Given the limitation from above, using LatentWorkers creates a long list of "worker" machines in the buildbot interface, one worker for each environment that actually *can* run on any particular physical machine. This list offers no real value and causes confusion. It also makes it very hard to:
** Isolate a physical machine temporarily from the build system (for other uses, such as performance testing).
** Dynamically scale resources up and down without rewriting the configuration.
* Balancing resources becomes problematic, as one must use buildbot {{Locks}}, but locks are *not shared* across multiple masters. This can lead to over allocating builds to machines from different masters, timing out the system.
* It also makes it hard to properly prioritise certain builds, unless they also get allocated to specific physical machines (as is the case for branch-protection builders).
* *Requires the use of "Trigger" steps to be able to change environments. This forces creation of more builders when an environment change is needed during a test step.*

h3. Technical changes

This task will require the addition of a "wrapper" class {{RunInDocker}} that wraps any particular shell command inside a:
{{docker run <env-parameters> <command>}}

This task does not cover migrating all builders to use this class. For evaluating completeness, there will be two builders that will be migrated to this class first:
* Latest Debian at time of implementation (Debian 12 or 13)
* Latest RHEL at time of implementation (RHEL 9 or RHEL 10)

h4. File sharing between test steps
As with this architecture, the environment is preserved between test steps, there will need to be another method employed.
* We will be leveraging specific folders on the physical machines, that will be mounted as volumes for all builder test steps.
* For certain cases there will be an {{autofs}} system mount, to share build artifacts across builders, much like it happens now with pushing packages to {{https://ci.mariadb.org}}.

h4. New challenges introduced by dropping DockerLatentWorker

h5. Cleanup pre and post builder runs
We have the following guarantee given buildbot's internal builder architecture:
* Any builder can not run in parallel on the same physical machine. Thus containers can have a particular name prefix to identify the corresponding builder.
** For example, for amd64-debian-12, we can use container names:
{{debian-12_<uuid>}}

Given this, the solution is:
* When a test starts we clean up any potentially hanging containers by prefix matching their name.
* When a test ends (or is canceled gracefully), we clean up any remaining running containers by prefix matching their name.

h5. Not overwriting other build files
* Shared artifacts between test steps will use a unique path, referencing the builder name and build number.
* Cleanup of previous artifacts will be done similarly to how containers are cleaned and removed.

h5. Changes in requirements on physical machines environment
Compared to previous setup, a worker machine will have to have the following packages installed:
# Docker daemon, with the socket accessible to the buildbot worker process. (Docker was previously required as well, but was controlled via the buildbot master)
# Buildbot worker process running (python3 virtualenv running internally, possibly twisted too)

fields.summary: faster distance calculations via extrapolation

issuetype.description: A new feature of the product, which has yet to be developed.
issuetype.name: New Feature

fields.description:
continue the work done with Eigen, but

* remove randomization (so, Eigen won't be needed)

* only use this optimization when dimensions *already* prepared for it
** e.g randomized in the client (Matryoshka?)

* automatically detect if this is the case:
** on inserts and on disk reads calculate the truncated and full distance, see if prediction works
** may be only of the first X% of rows (when reading into the cache)

comments.body:
*Speedup.* for dbpedia-openai-500k at (192, f=1.05) the speedup reaches 50% at recalls 0.9981–0.9983.
but generally varies from 1% to 53% with average about 30%

Less than I expected, but likely good to keep it

At f=1.10 the speedup is smaller, going down (f=1.03, f=1.02) doesn't bring additional speedup.

Randomized *mnist and gist show ~30% max.

gist benchmark runs in 18 hours, not in 30 hours.

For testing, the branch is bb-12.1-MDEV-36205-subdist and the feature itself has no configurable parameters cannot be explicitly enabled or disabled, it's not showing in EXPLAIN or anywhere else (will be, after MDEV-34805). It automatically kicks in on applicable datasets and makes inserts and searches somewhat faster.
pushed the test to provide some coverage

fields.summary: Remove amd64-debian-11-msan and last-N-failed from status reporting

issuetype.description: A task that needs to be done.
issuetype.name: Task

fields.description:
As per [~cvicentiu] request

*debian-11-msan* It will be replaced by a clang-20 builder in https://github.com/MariaDB/buildbot/pull/562 (cc: [~danblack] )
is not a protected branches builder, only reporting its status to GitHub and is causing unnecessary failures.
I will not create a separate Pull Request for it as its replacement is handled in MDBF-793 as mentioned,

*last-N-failed* is also only reporting its status and [~cvicentiu] reported often sporadic failures for it.

fields.description:
--binlog_row_metadata=full stores columns names and other metadata into the binary log.
However this is not used by replication threads, which can cause data loss on multi-master if one adds or drop fields with ALTER TABLE when binlog_format=row or binlog_format=statement is used.

ALTER TABLE will work if columns are added last to the table. However if one deletes columns or add a column in the middle of the table will cause all future DML to update wrong fields.

The fix is that if --binlog_row_metadata=full is used, we should not use field positions but instead use field names for insert and update when applying row events.
mariadb-binlog should also be update to show fieldnames instead of field positions if field names are available.

I will add a simple test case that one can use to verify the issue.

We should probably also add an option --slave_type_conversions=IGNORE_MISSING_COLUMNS to allow one to drop columns with ALTER TABLE

comments.body:
[~serg], [~elenst]:

I discussed this with Monty, and here is the summary of our chat:

The use case is limited to multi-master, with a distributed dataset where different masters update the same table but work on distinct ranges of data. So if one node runs an {{ALTER TABLE}} which re-arranges the order of the columns to be inconsistent with its master, then when that node replicates insert/update row events that target its altered table from its master, there will indeed be data loss. 

This should be fixed in 10.6, as we have many users/customers that run this topology running in 10.6, and the fix should be relatively easy with low risk. That is, to populate the fields of {{table->record[0]}} during unpacking using column names, rather than column indices. The patch applied in 10.6 should be relatively small; and any complex edge cases (e.g. enums) should just report as errors in 10.6, with fixes to be handled in newer versions. The patch in 10.6 can leverage ideas from the {{ONLINE ALTER}} work, and then in some 11.4+, the code can instead leverage the actual {{ONLINE ALTER}} code.

To the risk, this work will break functionality if a slave renames columns from its master. Currently, this use-case works as long as the column index is in the same location. With this patch, we will not be able to find the column on the slave-side table to write to. Monty says this is not a practical case though, and that users don't/wouldn't actually do this.
Adjusting remaining estimate to 2d for merging to {{main}} branch (MDEV-36892 will be involved, but has its own estimate)

items.toString: One can have data loss in multi-master setups when 1) both masters update the same table, 2) ALTER TABLE is run on one master which re-arranges the column ordering, and 3) transactions are binlogged in ROW binlog_format. This is because the slave assumes that all columns are in the same order on the master and slave and all columns on the master also exists on the slave. This feature fixes this when binlog_row_metadata=FULL is used on the master, by mapping fields via column_names rather than indices.
